# Plan — card 1861748259211445645: the SDK pilot cycle made mechanical

Base: develop f7d8d7e9. Sources read: `plugin/hooks-modules/sdk-pilot-lifecycle/hooks/hooks.js`, `plugin/bin/lib/pilot-runner-core.mjs`, `plugin/bin/wt-run-gate.mjs`, `plugin/bin/lib/gate-evidence.mjs`, `plugin/bin/wt-pilot-fidelity.mjs`, the two real runs of 2026-09-11 (`.claude/reports/sdk-lifecycle-1860610222/`, `.claude/reports/intake-triage-1860394456/`), the Sol review of the lifecycle card, ADR card 1859135211149723055 (dev lifecycle v1), ECC `phases.md` for the plan artifact shape.

## ADR (revision 3.1 — bound of three critic rounds reached; r3 findings R3-1/R3-2 applied by the arbiter without a fourth round; after critic rounds 1, 2 and 3 — `.lane/critic-r1.md`, `.lane/critic-r2.md`)

**Decision D0 — authority moves to the runner; the Function Hook keeps only the fences.** The critic proved from `hooks.js:1` that the hook sandbox has no Node: it cannot read a log reliably, cannot run git, cannot spawn. So the lifecycle state machine, every evidence check and every process launch live in a runner-hosted in-process MCP server (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` `createSdkMcpServer` + `tool()`, running inside the runner's Node process): tools `transition`, `write_artifact`, `run` (kinds `lane`, `gate`, `inspect`). The Function Hook `sdk-pilot-lifecycle` is reduced to a denylist/allowlist on harness tools: no Bash at all, Read/Glob/Grep refused outside the worktree by `realpath` (computed runner-side, passed to the hook as a fixed prefix) — the only job a hook can do without Node. Rejected: keep evidence checks in the hook (unprovable reads — critic F1, F5, F7).

**D1 — evidence is a file the RUNNER reads and hashes; a transition argument is a declaration.** Every edge names the file it requires under `<worktree>/.lane/`; the runner reads it, checks its terminal line, records `{path, size, sha256, mtime}` in `.lane/evidence.json`; the transition is accepted only against that attestation. No `gate_receipts` argument. Rejected: trust declarations (both real runs).

**D2 — the runner decides the route before `query()`, and passes it as IMMUTABLE server state.** `route-from-card.mjs` applies the ADR-v1 table (human `Route: LITE|FULL` line wins; FULL if effort ≥ M, type feature, a risk word, > 3 named files, or no DoD; doubt → FULL) and the per-phase models; `.lane/route.json` is written for AUDIT only, the server holds the values in memory. `discovery` refuses any other declaration with the reasons. (Critic F2, open question 1.)

**D3 — one lane per review phase, launched by the runner, attested by the runner.** `run {kind: 'lane', phase}` builds argv itself (launcher path, `--brief <root>/.lane/<phase>-brief.md`, `--log <root>/.lane/<phase>-run.log`, model from immutable state, timeout), spawns without a shell, waits, and attests the terminal `EXIT=` line, the log digest and the `<phase>-report.md` digest and size. Edges out of `tdd`, `critic`, `review`, `refutation`, `harden` require that attestation for THAT phase; `EXIT=124` or non-zero is accepted only as `changes-requested` with the log path in the reason; every outgoing edge of each of those phases is in the lock matrix, including `critic → plan`. (Critic F3, F12.)

**D4 — the plan is an artifact with checked sections, and its task list is quoted verbatim downstream.** `plan → critic` requires `.lane/plan.md` with `## ADR` (≥ 1 `Decision`, ≥ 1 `Rejected`), `## Tasks` (each with a `DoD:` line), `## Gates`; `critic → tdd` requires the critic lane's report to reference the plan digest; the `tdd` brief must contain the `## Tasks` block byte-identical (the runner compares the slice). Rejected: prose plan. (Critic F4, F11.)

**D5 — quality receipts are gate logs the runner produced and hashes.** `run {kind: 'gate', name}` runs `pnpm typecheck|lint|test` from `<root>/toolkit` detached, writes `.lane/<gate>.log` with the `EXIT=` marker, records digest + tree signature (`gate-evidence.mjs`, Node side). `verify passed` requires the three gate attestations with `EXIT=0`, taken after the last lane attestation, on the current tree signature; `report → awaiting_fidelity` requires the same digests and the same signature. (Critic F5, F13.)

**D6 — the runner commits, and the commit is part of the edge.** At `report → awaiting_fidelity` the runner records base HEAD, runs `git add -A` + `git commit -F` (subject = the pilot report's first line; body carries card id, SDK session id, tree signature, evidence.json digest), verifies HEAD moved and the tree is clean, records `commit` in `summary.json`; the transition is accepted only after that; a failed commit refuses the edge. (Critic F6, F14, open question 2.)

**D7 — no raw Bash, and no Read/Glob/Grep fence in the hook (critic N1).** The hook cannot resolve paths, so it fences nothing. Confinement is enforced by the RUNNER through the SDK `canUseTool` callback: for `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep` the runner resolves the requested path (`fs.realpathSync` on the deepest existing ancestor, then joins the remainder) and refuses anything whose real path is not under the worktree's real path; `cwd`-relative and `..` forms resolve the same way; a Glob/Grep `path` argument absent means the worktree. `run {kind: 'inspect'}` covers `git diff --stat`, `git status --short` and the tail of a named `.lane/` log with argv fixed server-side. `options.tools` = `['Read','Glob','Grep']` plus the MCP tools; the Function Hook module is deleted once the server carries the state machine. Rejected: a prefix check on the requested string (lexically inside, resolves outside).

**D8 — fidelity bundle hardening** with a canonical typed schema (`gate|lane|report|commit` entries, required fields, canonical JSON encoding), one snapshot id per freeze, length-prefixed fields; symlinks: `lstat` + `readlink`, record the link text, resolve the target against the root's real path, REFUSE the freeze when it escapes (never read through it); verifier round-trip lock. (Critic F8, F17, N7.)

**D10 — the tree signature excludes `.lane/` by construction (critic N4).** `gate-evidence.mjs treeSignature` enumerates `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`; `.lane/` is git-ignored in every card worktree, so evidence, logs and `evidence.json` never enter the signature. The runner asserts that at start (`git check-ignore .lane` must succeed) and refuses to run otherwise. Signature comparisons are taken on the same enumeration; nothing else is excluded.

**D9 — every refusal names edge, missing item and path**; locks are a table over every refusal, not a forbidden regex. (Critic F9, F15.)

**Order (critic F20, open question 3): the runner-hosted server with `run` lands FIRST**, replacing the Bash fence in one step; per-phase lanes are enabled in the same increment. The expanded-string-fence intermediate state never exists.

## Tasks

### Lane A — the runner-hosted lifecycle server (Terra, one worktree, tasks in THIS order; no intermediate state weaker than today because the old hook stays untouched until T-A6 swaps it out in one commit)
- A0 probes. DoD: three archived probe runs under `.lane/probes/` with pass criteria: P1 an in-process `createSdkMcpServer` tool appears in `system:init` AND a call to it from the pilot mutates state held in the runner process (a counter read back after the run) — proves shared state; P2 `canUseTool` in the runner receives `Read` with a path outside the worktree and refusing it is visible in the transcript as a denied tool result; P3 `spawn` with argv (no shell) from a tool handler runs the launcher and the handler observes its exit code. A failed probe stops the lane with the observation.
- A1 server skeleton. DoD: `plugin/bin/lib/sdk-pilot-lifecycle-server.mjs` exports `createLifecycleServer({worktree, route, models, cardId, sessionTag})` returning the SDK MCP server with tools `transition`, `write_artifact`, `run`; state is a closure over CONSTRUCTOR arguments (route and models immutable, `Object.freeze`); `.lane/route.json` written once for audit and never read back; unit locks on the fake seam for every edge of the state table (same table as today's hook, plus `critic → plan`), serialised transitions, idempotent `tool_use_id`.
- A2 route. DoD: `route-from-card.mjs` (ADR-v1 table; human `Route:` line wins; each FULL trigger alone; LITE only when all clear; doubt → FULL) with the two real card files of 2026-09-11 as fixtures (LSP → LITE, triage → FULL); `discovery` refuses a mismatching declaration naming the reasons.
- A3 `run` tool and per-phase lanes. DoD: `run {kind:'lane', phase}` builds argv (launcher, `--brief <root>/.lane/<phase>-brief.md`, `--log <root>/.lane/<phase>-run.log`, model from constructor state, timeout), spawns without shell, waits, attests `{path,size,sha256,mtime}` of the log (terminal `EXIT=` line required) and of `<phase>-report.md` into `.lane/evidence.json`; admitted in `tdd`, `critic`, `review`, `refutation`, `harden`; `run {kind:'gate', name}` for `typecheck|lint|test` from `<root>/toolkit`, writes `.lane/<gate>.log` with the marker and attests it plus the tree signature; `run {kind:'inspect', what}` for the three read-only commands. `wt-lane.mjs` gains `--log` and `--brief` (already `--brief`; add `--log`). Locks: every outgoing edge of each lane phase in a matrix (missing log · log without EXIT · EXIT=124 → only `changes-requested` with the path in the reason · non-zero → same · empty report), a `kind` outside the enum, a `phase` outside the current one.
- A4 evidence on edges. DoD: `tdd→verify`, `harden→verify`, `critic→tdd`, `critic→plan`, `review→*`, `refutation→*` require the phase's lane attestation; `verify passed` requires the three gate attestations with `EXIT=0`, newer than the last lane attestation, same tree signature; `report→awaiting_fidelity` requires the same digests and signature; `gate_receipts` and `findings`-only declarations removed from the schema where an attestation replaces them; `D10` start assertion (`.lane` ignored). Locks red per requirement.
- A5 plan artifact and briefs. DoD: `write_artifact` kinds and the ONLY phase each is admitted in: `plan` (plan), `critic-brief` (plan, after plan.md exists), `brief` (tdd), `review-brief` (review), `refutation-brief` (refutation), `harden-brief` (harden), `pilot-report` (report — written BEFORE the transition; critic R3-1); `plan→critic` requires `plan.md` with `## ADR` (≥1 Decision, ≥1 Rejected), `## Tasks` (each with `DoD:`), `## Gates`; `critic→tdd` requires the critic report to contain the plan's sha256 (the runner injects it into the critic brief) and the tdd `brief` to contain the `## Tasks` block byte-identical; locks red on each.
- A6 commit inside the edge, archive, and the swap. DoD: `report→awaiting_fidelity` requires `.lane/pilot-report.md` present (written in `report`); the runner records base HEAD, stages and commits (`-F` message: subject = report first line; body: card id, SDK session id, tree signature, evidence.json sha256), verifies HEAD moved and tree clean, writes `commit` into `summary.json`; then COPIES the whole `.lane/` (receipts, logs, evidence.json, plan, briefs, reports) to `<project>/.claude/reports/<card-id>-<run-stamp>/` with a manifest keyed by card, route, commit, phase list, evidence.json sha256 (critic R3-2: receipts are git-ignored and must outlive the worktree); failure of commit or archive refuses the edge (locks: failed commit, unchanged HEAD, dirty tree, commit-before-transition ordering). Same commit: the runner passes `options.tools`, `canUseTool` confinement (D7) and the server; the old `sdk-pilot-lifecycle` hook module and its tests are removed; `pilot-runner-core.mjs` no longer loads it. Refusal messages per D9 with a table lock over every refusal (edge, missing item, path).

### Lane B — fidelity bundle hardening (Terra, after lane A)
- B1. DoD: the four D8 items, each with a red lock; verifier round-trip; symlink escape refuses the freeze.

### Lane C — documents and the real runs (main-driven)
- C1 docs. DoD: PILOT-RUNNER.md describes the evidence table per edge, the `run` tool and `canUseTool` confinement; PILOT-CONTRACT.md ≤ 6144 bytes names the artifacts the pilot must produce; CHANGELOG Unreleased, one bullet per behaviour-changing decision.
- C2 real runs. DoD: one LITE and one FULL real card through the runner on develop; archive manifest per run keyed by card, route, commit, phase list, evidence.json sha256; the FULL run shows critic, review and refutation lanes with their attestations; this card's own review goes through the mechanism (its FULL run IS the review).

## Gates
Per lane, from `<worktree>/toolkit`, detached, each with an `EXIT=` last line: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`; `node plugin/bin/wt-plugin-validate.mjs --strict` (or the `claude plugin validate` equivalent used today); `git diff --check`. Every lock proven red first, archived at `.lane/red/<task>-<lock>.log` with its `EXIT=` line. Test-union: total after each lane strictly greater than before. Review: Sol on a repository-free diff bundle after lane A and after lane B; refutation lane; dispositions on the card; main's diff-read and one recorded gate on develop after the merge.

## Critic round 3 answers, applied
- `canUseTool`: used only if A0/P2 proves it runs under the runner's bypass settings; the lifecycle MCP tool names are exact-allowed; malformed built-in inputs fail closed; relative paths resolve from the worktree; symlink targets resolved.
- The single-commit swap is atomic in history only: A6 adds a startup handshake — the runner refuses to start unless exactly one lifecycle implementation is present (server registered, old hook module absent), and `summary.json` records the implementation version.

## Former open questions (closed)
1. Is `canUseTool` the right confinement point for Read/Glob/Grep, given it also receives every MCP tool call (must allow ours)?
2. Does A6's single-commit swap leave any window where a run could start with neither the old hook nor the new server?
